twla-visual-tactile-clocks-v1.alt: Several tactile updates fall between two visual updates on a timeline. Below it, the visual branch feeds the tactile editor, which outputs the corrected action chunk.
twla-visual-tactile-clocks-v1.caption: A visual update caches the base chunk until the next visual update. Between them, tactile updates use recent touch and elapsed time to correct it. Spacing illustrates the sequence. Measured rates and performance are reported separately.
twla-visual-tactile-clocks-v1.changes: Independently drawn explanatory diagram with English labels.

twla-valid-unexecuted-residual-v1.alt: Gray positions have executed, amber positions are valid and pending, and red positions are invalid padding. A residual arrow points only to the amber portion of the cached base chunk.
twla-valid-unexecuted-residual-v1.caption: The current residual applies only to valid, unexecuted positions of the same cached base chunk. Executed positions and padding are excluded. This is an explanatory diagram.
twla-valid-unexecuted-residual-v1.changes: Independently drawn explanatory diagram with English labels.

trex-figure3-model-architecture.alt: T-Rex architecture. Above are latent, action and tactile experts with shared attention. Below, the action expert runs steps 0–6 and hands an intermediate noisy action to the tactile expert through step 10. At right, T-Rex labels the rates around 5 and 20 Hz.
trex-figure3-model-architecture.caption: In T-Rex, a fast tactile expert refines the intermediate action representation produced by slower action computation. The figure describes the prior T-Rex system.
trex-figure3-model-architecture.credit: Figure 3 from Niu et al., “T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation,” arXiv:2606.17055v2, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17055v2, CC BY 4.0. Used unmodified.

flora-original-figure-1.alt: A robot stacks cups. The timeline shows action segments and captions, with outcome, progress, and criterion-based ratings below.
flora-original-figure-1.caption: The upper panel labels the segments in a cup-stacking video and describes each action. The lower panel shows three ways to score the task.

flora-original-figure-5.credit: Leng et al. · FLORA: An Open Model Suite for Scaling Robotics Data Engines · Figure 5 · arXiv:2610.31779v1
flora-original-figure-5.alt: The panels compare event boundaries and model scores, captions for inserting a wire and moving tea leaves, an assembly failure, and partial progress after a bottle falls.
flora-original-figure-5.caption: Selected examples compare segment detection, captions, failure judgments, and partial progress. The model names and individual panel scores are reproduced from the original figure.

cacheflex-vector-width-unit.alt: Four 64-byte blocks fit side by side across the width of a single 256-byte vector.
cacheflex-vector-width-unit.caption: At VL=16 the 256-byte vector spans four 64-byte cache lines. The diagram compares widths and gives no transaction count or speedup.
